def: The tendency of distances to become similar and data to become sparse as the number of dimensions grows, which weakens neighbour and density methods.
A linear method that finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance and projects the data onto the first few of them.
One of the orthogonal directions found by PCA, ordered by how much variance the data has along it.
The share of the total variance in the data that lies along a principal component.
A plot of the variance explained by each principal component in order, used to decide how many to keep.
The weights with which the original columns combine to form a principal component.
The difference between the original data and its approximation from a reduced number of components.
A non-linear embedding that places points in two dimensions so that neighbour probabilities match those in the original space, preserving local structure.
The t-SNE setting that fixes the effective number of neighbours each point considers, typically between 5 and 50.
The lack of room in a low-dimensional map for all the moderately distant neighbours a point has in high dimensions.
A non-linear embedding that builds a fuzzy nearest-neighbour graph and finds a low-dimensional layout with a matching graph, faster than t-SNE and able to transform new points.
